raw_statement: I was driving my silver 2023 Honda Civic EX (license TX-MKL-4927, VIN 2HGFE2F59PH512847, mileage is around 28,450) southbound on Congress Avenue approaching West 5th Street around 8:15 AM yesterday (Sept 14, 2026). The light went yellow, so I brought the car to a normal stop. While waiting at the red, a white Ford F-150 smashed into my rear end out of nowhere at full speed. It knocked me forward about half a car length into the pedestrian crosswalk. My seatbelt violently locked and jerked me backward. When I got out, the rear bumper was totally caved in and split down the middle, the trunk lid is crunched upwards and won't latch shut at all, and both tail light lenses are completely shattered. The metal panels on both sides above the rear wheels are dented in, especially the left side. The truck driver was James T. Whitfield (State Farm policy SF-9928-TX-441, plate TX-BRN-7712). He was apologetic and said he was looking down at his GPS on his phone. APD Officer Daniel Reyes (Badge 4418) responded to the scene and filed report APD-2026-091421. I refused EMS at the scene, but my neck got really stiff and painful that night, so I went to Austin Family Medicine to see Dr. Priya Sharma this morning. She diagnosed me with acute cervical strain and gave me muscle relaxants. The car can still drive forward, but the trunk is tied down with bungee cords and the rear lights don't work.
